question: Who established Shantiniketan and when?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravindranath Tagore, 1901**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** established Shantiniketan as an experimental school aimed at blending the best of Western and Indian educational systems.
 
• Shantiniketan was founded in **1901** in the Birbhum district of West Bengal, India.
 
• The school was later expanded and developed into **Visva-Bharati University** in 1921.
 
• Shantiniketan became a center for cultural, artistic, and educational activities, attracting students and scholars from all over the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**

 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a renowned poet, writer, composer, and philosopher from India.
 
• He was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his work "Gitanjali".
 
• Tagore's contributions to literature, music, and art have had a profound impact on Indian culture and beyond.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Bard of Bengal" and is best known for his poetry and songs, including the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Visva-Bharati University**
 
 
• Visva-Bharati University was founded by Rabindranath Tagore in 1921 as a center for higher learning and research.
 
• The university is located in Shantiniketan, West Bengal, and is known for its unique approach to education, emphasizing the harmony between man and nature.
 
• It offers a wide range of programs in humanities, social sciences, science, music, fine arts, and performing arts.
 
• Visva-Bharati continues to attract students and scholars from around the world, maintaining its legacy as a place of cultural and intellectual exchange.
 
 
 
• **Shantiniketan**
 
 
• Shantiniketan, meaning "Abode of Peace", was originally an ashram built by Rabindranath Tagore's father, Maharshi Devendranath Tagore.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore expanded Shantiniketan into an experimental school with an emphasis on natural surroundings, creativity, and learning through exploration.
 
• Shantiniketan later evolved into Visva-Bharati University, becoming a prominent center for education and cultural activities.
 
• The place remains a symbol of Tagore's vision of a holistic and inclusive education system.
